subject: Recap & next steps — Cygnus engagement: scope, success metrics, and initial access
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cygnus.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Cygnus engagement: scope, success metrics, and initial access

Hi Alex —

Great conversation today — thanks for the time. Below is a short recap plus proposed next steps so we can get the engagement started next week. I focused this on the pilot scope we discussed and the minimum access we'll need to run the prompt/eval suite.

1) Goal and scope
- Primary goal: reduce triage time for Cygnus support tickets by ~40% using an LLM assistant for first-touch summarization and routing.
- Pilot scope: 6-week sprint; evaluate on support queue for Product A (US region). Train/evaluate on 10k historical ticket snippets + rolling stream for live evaluation.

2) Success metrics (agreed)
- Accuracy: >= 85% label agreement vs SME on routing decisions (sampled evals)
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 450ms per inference for the pre-processing + classification path
- Business impact: 30–40% reduction in mean time to triage in pilot window (measured vs baseline).

3) Owners (who does what)
- Cygnus: Alex — dataset access, SME availability for weekly eval review; Procurement — contract & PO
- Redwood: Jonas — engagement lead; Kimberly — infra & access; Grace — eval plan & prompt set curation

4) Initial access & infra needs (what we need from Cygnus)
- SFTP or GCS share with historical ticket exports (CSV, gz ok) — samples and full export for first 10k rows; details in attachment.
- Temporary read-only API key for support system (or a sanitized export cadence) to enable live stream evaluation.
- Whitelisted IP ranges for private pilot endpoints (we will send the CIDR block).
- Point contact for SOC/compliance questionnaire (we'll need evidence for audit logs and retention policy).

5) Prompt/eval plan highlights
- We'll start with a 30-prompt seed set baked from your top 200 ticket templates; refine via 3 iterative eval rounds.
- We'll run automated A/B prompt comparisons and create a lightweight human-in-the-loop review dashboard for discrepant cases.

6) Timeline (proposed)
- Tue 26 May: secure data export + procurement kickoff
- Wed 27 May: access & infra setup (whitelisting, temp keys)
- Thu 28 May: baseline ingest + initial prompt set run
- Mon 01 Jun: first evaluation review and calibration workshop

Next steps (please confirm):
- Alex: confirm you can share the 10k ticket sample by Tue 26 May and provide the SOC contact.
- Procurement: share standard PO cadence; we can accept a short-term pilot SOW while contract is finalizing.

Attachments: cygnus-mrp-access-stub.pdf (sample layout), pilot-success-metrics.xlsx (metric templates)

Thanks — I’ll loop Kimberly on the infra notes and Grace will share the eval template tomorrow.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cygnus.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cygnus.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Cygnus engagement: scope, success metrics, and initial access

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear write-up, appreciated. A few quick items from our side:

- Confirmed: we can export 10k historical ticket rows (anonymized) by end of day Tue 26 May. I will drop them into a temp GCS bucket and send credentials via secure link.
- SOC contact: that would be Priya Rao (priya.rao@cygnus.ai). She’ll expect a short evidence packet (logs + retention policy).
- Procurement: we typically need an SOW + short PO. Procurement is cc'd.

Couple questions:
1) For the latency target, is the 450ms target measured exclusive of network egress time? Our infra will be in us-central1.
2) For the whitelisting — can you send the exact CIDR(s) you need? Security will only allow one change window next week.

If all that aligns I’m good to proceed with the pilot SOW. Can we do the calibration workshop on Mon 1 Jun at 10am PT?

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product — Support Automation | Cygnus Analytics
alex.chen@cygnus.ai
+1 (206) 555-0182

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@cygnus.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 19:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Cygnus engagement: scope, success metrics, and initial access

Alex —

Quick answers:
- Latency: our 95th percentile target is measured at the service edge (Redwood inference runtime) — excludes client network variability. We’ll include an agent-side timing sample to help you separate network egress from inference time.
- CIDR: sending the minimal block now — 34.216.120.0/24 (expected change window Wed 27 May). If you need a ticket for your firewall team I can attach our security form.

Also attaching a short checklist for the temporary API keys and a sample ingestion manifest (csv columns we need). I’ll coordinate with Priya on SOC evidence packet next week.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Engineering Lead, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference

Alex / team —

Thanks — this all looks good. Confirming the calibration workshop for Mon 1 Jun at 10am PT. I’ll create a short agenda (30–45m): walkthrough of seed prompt set, expected sampling cadence, and first-look dashboards.

Action items I own before the workshop:
- Send the workshop agenda + invite (by Mon 25 May)
- Provision a temporary pilot namespace in us-central1 and share the whitelisted endpoint + sample timing tool (by Wed 27 May)
- Grace will pre-populate the first 30 prompt templates and share the scoring rubric by end of day Thu 28 May

Alex — once you drop the GCS bucket link I’ll validate the sample and confirm ingestion. Procurement: happy to accept a short pilot SOW; Jonas will own the initial scope and we can convert to a longer-term contract after acceptance.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting started.

—Jonas
